sourceSentences.text: ‘Shut up!
Shut up!’
Etta’s voice slid up the scale, cracking on hysteria.
She slapped Althea, an open-handed blow that rang in the confined companionway.
‘Etta!
Stop that, I said!’
Kennit cried in horror.
He seized the whore’s upraised hand by the wrist and tried to drag her off Althea.
Instead, Etta only struck her with her other hand, and then, to Kennit’s complete mystification, burst into tears.
Kennit lifted his eyes to find half a dozen sailors crowding the end of the hall, staring in open-mouthed wonder at the spectacle.
‘Separate them,’ he snapped.
Finally, several men moved forwards to do his bidding.
Wintrow took Etta by the arm and pulled her from Althea.
For a wonder, she did not fight him, but allowed him to hold her back.
‘Put Etta in my chamber until she calms herself,’ he directed Wintrow.
‘You others, put Althea back in her room and fasten the lock.
I will deal with her later.’
Althea’s brief struggle with Etta had consumed her resistance.
Her eyes were open, but her head lolled on her neck as two men dragged her to her feet.
‘I’ll … kill… you,’ she promised him gaspingly as they hauled her past him.
She meant it.
He drew his handkerchief from his pocket and dabbed at his brow.
The blood on the cloth was darker; the cut was clotting.
He probably looked a sight.
The prospect of confronting Etta did not appeal to him, but it could not be avoided.
He would not walk about with blood dribbling down his face and spattered food on his clothing.
He drew himself up straight.
As the crewmen returned from locking Althea up, he managed a wry smile for them.
He shook his head conspiratorially.
‘Women.
They simply do not belong aboard a ship.’
One crewman returned him a grin, but the others looked uneasy.
That was not good.
Was Etta that great a favourite with the crew?
He’d have to do something about that.
He’d have to do something about this whole situation.
How had it become so untidy?
He straightened his rumpled jacket and brushed food from the sleeve.
‘Captain Kennit, sir?’
He looked up in annoyance at yet another rattled deckhand.
‘What is it now?’ he snapped.
The man licked his lips.
‘It’s the ship, sir.
The figurehead.
She says she wants to see you, sir.’
The sailor swallowed, and then went on, ‘She said, “Tell him right now.
Now!”
No disrespect intended, sir, but that was how she spoke, sir.’
‘Did she?’
Kennit managed to keep his voice coolly amused.
‘Well, you may tell her, with no disrespect intended, that the captain has another matter to tend to, but that he will be with her presently.
At his earliest convenience.’
‘Sir!’
The man fumbled for a way to begin a desperate protest.
Kennit speared him with a cold gaze.
‘Yes, sir,’ he conceded.
His step dragged as he departed.
Kennit did not envy him his errand, but he could scarcely let the ship see him like this, let alone have a common seaman see him dash to obey the ship’s summons.
He lifted a hand to smooth his moustache.
‘Slow.
Calm.
Steady.
Take control of it again,’ he counselled himself.
But a tiny voice spoke from his wrist in mocking counterpoint.
‘Swiftly.
Messily.
It all falls to pieces.
In the end, dear sir, you will not even have control of yourself.
No more than Igrot did when he met his fate at your hands.
For when you became the beast, little Kennit, you doomed yourself to share the beast’s end.’
‘Etta.
Etta, please,’ Wintrow begged her, helplessly torn.
He should be seeing to Althea.
She had appeared both sick and deranged, but how could he leave Etta like this?
She paid no attention.
She wept on, sobbing into the pillows as if she could not stop.
He had never seen anyone weep this way.
There was a terrible violence to her gasping sobs, as if her body sought to purge herself of sorrow, but the misery went too deep for tears to assuage.
‘Etta, please, Etta,’ he tried again.
She did not even seem to hear him.
Timidly, he patted her on the back.
He had dim memories of his mother patting his little sister so, when Malta was so immersed in a tantrum that she could not calm herself.
‘There, there,’ he said comfortingly.
‘It’s all over now.
It’s all over.’
He moved his hand in a small, comforting circle.

Припини, я сказав!

Він витяг з кишені носовичок і промокнув чоло.

Мабуть, вигляд він мав ще той.

Це було недобре.
Невже Етта така велика улюблениця команди?
Треба буде щось із цим робити.
Треба буде щось робити з усією цією ситуацією.

Він розправив зім’ятий камзол і змахнув їжу з рукава.

Він роздратовано звів очі на ще одного розгубленого матроса.

Носова фігура.

Матрос ковтнув і повів далі: — Вона сказала: «Скажіть йому просто зараз.

Кеннітові вдалося зберегти в голосі холодну насмішку.

Спокійно.
Рівно.
Знову візьми все під контроль, — порадив він собі.

— Швидко.
Брудно.
Усе розпадається на шматки.
Зрештою, любий сер, ви не матимете влади навіть над собою.
Не більшої, ніж мав Іґрот, коли зустрів свою долю від ваших рук.

— Етто.

Йому слід було подбати про Альтею.
Вона здавалася водночас хворою й божевільною, та як він міг покинути Етту в такому стані?
Вона не звертала на нього уваги.
Вона все плакала, ридаючи в подушки, наче не могла зупинитися.
Він ніколи не бачив, щоб хтось плакав так.
У її судомних риданнях була жахлива лють, наче її тіло прагнуло вивергнути із себе горе, але страждання залягло надто глибоко, щоб сльози могли його вгамувати.
— Етто, будь ласка, Етто, — спробував він знову.
Здавалося, вона його навіть не чує.
Він несміливо погладив її по спині.
Він невиразно пам’ятав, як мати так само поплескувала його молодшу сестру, коли Мальта так поринала в напад вередування, що вже не могла себе заспокоїти.
— Ну-ну, — утішливо мовив він.
— Усе вже скінчилося.
Усе скінчилося.
Він повів рукою, описуючи невелике заспокійливе коло.
